title: Cardiovascular disease and risk; Dissection and tissue studies
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: PR05b#t2 term and clue written for the game; PR05b#t1 term and clue written for the game; EX13b#t4 term and clue written for the game; PR05a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EX13b#N.3, PR05b#N.11, EX13b#N.6, EX13b#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Vein
items.clue: Vessel with a thin wall that collapses flat.

items.label: Artery
items.clue: Vessel with a thick, elastic wall that stays open.

items.label: Reliability
items.clue: Shown by a finding when repeat studies give similar results.

items.label: Pith
items.clue: Tissue in the middle of a stem, inside the ring of vascular bundles.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. In a study of 20 countries, the correlation coefficient between mean saturated fat intake and the death rate from coronary heart disease was +0.85. What can be concluded from this result alone?

options.text: There is a strong positive correlation between the variables, but this does not prove that one causes the other.
Saturated fat in the diet is shown to cause coronary heart disease, because the coefficient is so close to +1, the maximum.
The relationship is weak, because a correlation calculated from only 20 countries cannot be a strong one.
Saturated fat from food coats the inside of the coronary arteries, which is why the two variables rise together in step.

questions.stem: A student dissects a set of sheep's lungs. Near the lungs she finds two tubes side by side. Tube P has C-shaped rings of cartilage in its wall and stays open when empty. Tube Q has a thin, soft wall with no cartilage and collapses flat. Which identification do these observations best support?

options.text: P is an artery: it has the thicker wall and stays open, as arteries do.
P is a bronchus, held open by its cartilage; Q is a blood vessel.
Q is an artery: blood at high pressure needs a wide, soft-walled vessel.
Q is a vein, because it carries blood that is low in oxygen.

questions.explanation: Structure identifies it: C-shaped cartilage keeps airways open. A thin wall that collapses fits a vein, such as a pulmonary vein.

questions.stem: Early epidemiological studies found that women taking HRT had a lower incidence of coronary heart disease (CHD). Later randomised controlled trials found that HRT slightly increased CHD risk. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The early studies were correct because they involved far more women than the trials did, so their result should be preferred.
The correlation was not causal: women on HRT tended to have higher socioeconomic status, which itself lowers CHD risk.
HRT must lower CHD risk in most women, and the trials must have happened to sample an unusual group of women.
The early correlation must have been a chance result: women on HRT did not really have lower CHD rates.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. A study of 2000 adults found a correlation coefficient of −0.40 between hours of golf played per week and the incidence of coronary heart disease. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Playing golf probably protects against coronary heart disease, since the correlation shows that more golf goes with less disease.
There is almost no relationship, because a negative coefficient always shows a weak link between two variables.
The relationship must be strong, since it was measured in 2000 people and sample size shows how strong a link is.
More golf goes with less disease, moderately; a confounder such as income may explain it, so cause is not shown.
